teams.heading: Fiji surrender Pacific Nations Cup title following defeat to Japan in Tokyo
teams.body: Fiji surrendered their Pacific Nations Cup crown in Tokyo on Saturday, falling 20-15 to Japan in a tense final. Despite leading 12-10 at half-time through tries from Virimi Vakatawa and captain Tevita Ikanivere, the Flying Fijians struggled after the break. Halfback Frank Lomani lamented second-half mistakes and a defensive drop-off that allowed Samisoni Tua to score the winning try for the hosts. Fiji were starved of the ball, managing just 36 per cent possession and conceding 14 penalties as their title defence unravelled in the final 10 minutes.

lead.why: The Pacific Nations Cup final defeat to Japan is the major international result and the weekend's dominant story for the Flying Fijians.

teams.heading: Canada hold England women to draw as 39-match winning streak ends
teams.body: The Red Roses’ record-breaking run of 39 consecutive victories concluded on Saturday following a dramatic 26-26 draw against Canada at Sandy Park. John Mitchell’s side twice recovered from behind in the first half through a Claudia Moloney-MacDonald brace, but they were eventually pegged back by a late Olivia Apps try. While England remain unbeaten in 40 Tests, the result marks the first time they have failed to win since the 2022 World Cup final. The two sides meet again for two Tests in Canada next month.

lead.why: The conclusion of the Red Roses' historic 39-game winning run is the most significant and widely covered event in the pack.

teams.heading: France women stage miraculous comeback win after trailing Australia by nineteen points
teams.body: France women orchestrated an extraordinary 29-26 victory over the Wallaroos in Aix-en-Provence on Saturday after overcoming a 19-point deficit and being reduced to just 11 players during a chaotic first half. On a bizarre afternoon featuring a second-half delay due to a burning bus adjacent to the Stade Maurice David, the fourth-ranked hosts reeled off 17 unanswered points in the final 25 minutes. Wallaroos coach Tim Walsh admitted post-match that his side failed to execute after putting themselves in a winning position.

lead.why: France women's extraordinary comeback win against Australia dominated the weekend rugby coverage.

teams.heading: Scott Bemand laments missed opportunity as Ireland surrender 19-point lead against USA
teams.body: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand admitted Sunday's 40-36 defeat against USA in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won." His side raced into a 31-12 advantage following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald, Aoife Wafer, Eve Higgins and Erin King. However, a second-half loss of discipline—compounded by Elmes Kinlan's yellow card—allowed Jack Hanratty's Eagles to storm back with four successive tries, leaving Ireland scrambling in vain when Dorothy Wall crossed in the red.

lead.why: Scott Bemand's frank post-match assessment of the WXV opening defeat to USA leads the rugby press today.

teams.heading: Italy women dominate Japan with a fifty-five to twenty-one victory
teams.body: The Italy women's team opened their WXV Global Series campaign in style on Sunday, defeating Japan 55-21 at Stadio Omero Tognon. Emma Stevanin set the tone early with a cross-kick for Aura Muzzo to score, before tries from Alessandra Frangipani, Alyssa D'Inca, Vittoria Vecchini and Giordana Duca built a commanding lead. Captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi marked her 50th cap by crossing for a score, sealing a convincing victory in their tournament opener.

teams.heading: Scotland women suffer heavy defeat against rampant New Zealand at Hive Stadium
teams.body: Scotland endured a difficult afternoon at Hive Stadium as New Zealand ran in 10 tries to secure a comfortable victory in the WXV Global Series. Evie Gallagher crossed twice in the first half to provide some resistance for the hosts, but the Black Ferns' relentless tempo and superior finishing exposed defensive frailties before the break. Despite keeping the visitors scoreless for a long spell in the second half, the Scots ultimately slipped to a second successive defeat in the tournament.

teams.heading: Sean Lynn guides Wales women to stunning victory over South Africa
teams.body: Wales delivered an eight-try masterclass to crush South Africa 50-19 in their WXV Global Series opener at Cardiff Arms Park. Sean Lynn's side raced into a 38-5 half-time lead, shaking off years of criticism with a fearless display of attacking rugby. Sisilia Tuipulotu bagged a dominant double, while co-captain Alex Callender capped a player-of-the-match performance with a late score in the corner. "This is just the start for us, this is going to be our new DNA," Lynn said.

teams.heading: Carlo Tizzano targets South Africa scalp as Perth embraces sporting fever
teams.body: Wallabies flanker Carlo Tizzano has set his sights on defeating world champions South Africa in Perth, calling it the ultimate test of the team's recent growth under Les Kiss. Australia enter the fixture following a five-match unbeaten run, bolstered by a 34-man squad that includes uncapped recruit Harry McLaughlin-Phillips and the return of utility back Jordan Petaia. Tizzano noted that "South Africa are the best team in the world, so what better way to test what we've been doing and everything we've been working on than doing it against the best?".

teams.heading: Naoto Saito and Eddie Jones inspire Japan to historic Pacific Nations Cup final victory
teams.body: Japan secured a historic 20-15 victory over Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium to claim their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019. Having fallen short against the Flying Fijians in the previous two finals, Eddie Jones' side overturned a half-time deficit thanks to tries from Mamoru Harada, Ben Gunter and tournament player of the tournament Samisoni Tua. The triumph lifts the Brave Blossoms into the world's top 10 rankings as they build toward the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

lead.why: Eddie Jones' Japan defeated Fiji 20-15 to claim their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019.

teams.heading: Shane Howarth supports Super Rugby theory behind All Blacks scrum issues
teams.body: Former All Black Shane Howarth believes the national side's scrum problems stem from losing regular fixtures against South African franchises when they exited Super Rugby in 2020. Following a 3-1 series defeat to the Springboks where tighthead Tyrel Lomax and the set-piece particularly struggled, Howarth backed Neil Barnes' theory that New Zealand missed out on vital scrummaging exposure now housed in the United Rugby Championship. When asked if NZ Rugby policy preventing overseas-based players from representing the national team should change, Howarth replied, "You're not going to get an argument from me."

lead.why: Leading with Shane Howarth and Neil Barnes' assessment of Super Rugby's impact on the All Blacks' scrum struggles against South Africa.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus releases Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende early
teams.body: Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus has released flank Pieter-Steph du Toit and centre Damian de Allende from the squad ahead of next Sunday's one-off Test against the Wallabies in Perth. The two first-choice players are returning to South Africa to spend time with their families following a demanding workload during the recent Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series against the All Blacks. Erasmus confirmed that sufficient cover remains within the travelling squad for the fixture at Optus Stadium.
